rules.name: Distinct Hull & Rig Silhouette
rules.description: Every vessel class must be identifiable from its blacked-out silhouette alone by hull sheer, stem/sternpost rake, and mast/sail plan.

rules.name: Readable Deck & Maritime Scale Cues
rules.description: Include clear maritime scale anchors such as bulwark rail height, gunport spacing, companionway hatches, capstans, or ship's boat chocks.

rules.name: Honest Timber, Canvas, and Cordage Detail
rules.description: Planking seams, futtock knees, tarred hemp shrouds, and flax canvas reef bands must follow shipwright joinery rather than noisy greeble.

rules.name: Rigging & Sail-Plan Clarity
rules.description: Standing rigging (stays, shrouds) and primary propulsion (square sails, lateens, gaffs, or oar banks) must connect logically to spars and hull.

rules.name: Tradition-Authentic Hull Form
rules.description: Hull beam-to-length ratio, castle height, and bow entry must match the vessel's declared maritime tradition and merchant or naval role.

rules.name: Material Separation Across Hull, Spar, and Ironwork
rules.description: Pitch-sealed oak planking, oiled pine spars, weathered flax canvas, and forged iron chainplates or bronze fittings must read as distinct materials.

rules.name: Controlled Maritime Palette
rules.description: Limit each vessel to its tradition's timber, hull-paint, and sail-dye palette; avoid neon saturation or modern synthetic finishes.

rules.name: Earned Sea-Salt & Service Weathering
rules.description: Barnacle fouling at the waterline, salt crust on bows, sun-bleached canvas, and battle patches must follow water flow and wind exposure.

rules.name: Unclipped Masthead-to-Waterline Framing
rules.description: Frame the entire vessel from bowsprit tip to taffrail and keel/waterline to maintruck with breathing room around spars and rigging.

rules.name: Seaworthy Hydrostatic & Rig Balance
rules.description: Center of effort in the sail plan and hull buoyancy distribution must look physically seaworthy with coherent waterline trim.
